text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. envoy conveys ideas on how to settle the tension on the island.
- Turkey is planning an air and naval blockade of Cyprus at the beginning of April to stop the Russian made S-300 missiles arriving.
- Co-op audit service finds a series of irregularities relating to fund mismanagement in Co-Op Societies.
- Russia is ready for active involvement in the search for a solution to the Cyprus problem.
- The Cyprus Tourism Organisation is trying to disengage itself from over-dependence on large tour operators.
- U.S. envoy Carey Cavanaugh submits preconditions today for an initiative to start on the Cyprus problem.
- The government has started contacts with Britain for its troops to stop using areas of the Akamas peninsula as a firing range.
- War in April. The Turks are preparing air strikes against Cyprus while the US expects a Greco-Turkish confrontation will last for three days in the Aegean and on Cyprus.
- Central Bank board is due to announce an interest rate cut on January 16th.
